answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock a 100-credit bond for 30 days before receiving a quota of ten requests per hour. Agents named sable, falcon, and pearl follow the same rule. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 credits; splitting one bond across aliases earns no extra quota. This does not prove identities are unique, but it makes sybil capacity scale with committed capital rather than free account creation.
